finding: LLaMAR publishes first-party evidence for the exact disturbance used by canonical S2=A: in MAP-THOR, moving from three robots to four/five slightly reduces success and transport despite increasing coverage, and the paper attributes the decline to crowding, blocking and collisions. The native actor/controller also contains the anti-blocking coordination relation, but the published experiments do not provide a matched treatment that disables/enables that relation while holding the rest of the system fixed. The result therefore corroborates the S2 disturbance boundary but is not a direct attenuation observation.
reassess_if: LLaMAR publishes an immutable matched ablation that disables or changes the native anti-blocking/interference attenuation relation while holding the remaining system materially fixed
a public matched benchmark directly evaluates LLaMAR native S2 against another canonical native S2 system under one disturbance definition
